title: Phishing messages worksheet
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Selection in physical computing and Secure Your Secrets
source: Seeded from computing/y5 lesson 5 (Phishing messages worksheet (pupil PDF; all messages invented by the school))
intro: Lesson 5: Secure your secrets: passwords, personal information and phishing. To understand how to keep personal information secure and spot a phishing message

questions.q: Find two warning signs: 'URGENT!!! Your acount will be deleted. Type your password here.'
questions.a: Urgency and a request for the password (also the spelling 'acount').
questions.model: Teacher reads it aloud and underlines: 'URGENT' (rushing you), 'acount' (spelling mistake), 'type your password' (asks for a secret).

questions.q: Is your favourite colour personal information to keep private?
questions.a: Not usually: it does not identify you or unlock anything.

questions.q: Who do you tell about a phishing message?
Core: Read the three messages on the worksheet. Mark each 'safe' or 'phishing' and give one reason.
questions.a: 1 phishing (prize and password), 2 safe (lesson reminder), 3 phishing (urgent link).

questions.q: Extend: Write a 'Secure your secrets' rule card with 4 rules in the portal response box.
questions.a: For example: never share passwords; check before clicking; first name only in Teams; tell a trusted adult.

questions.q: Stretch: Write a reply plan for a friend who has clicked a phishing link.
questions.a: Tell a parent now, change the password with a parent, tell the teacher, do not click again.

questions.q: Phishing is... A) a hobby B) a fake message that tricks you C) a strong password
questions.a: B) a fake message that tricks you
options: A fake message that tricks you

questions.q: Name one warning sign of phishing.
questions.a: For example: asks for a password, rushes you, too good to be true.
